title: Skewer a king and queen
objective: Use a rook check to expose a queen on the same file, then capture it.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original practice lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original practice position and teaching text; not a historical game

steps.explanation: Black's king on d5 stands in front of the queen on d8. Put your rook on their file with check. This is a skewer: the king shields the piece behind it.

question.prompt: Give a rook check on the king and queen's file.
hints: Both targets are on the d-file.
Move the rook from a1 to d1.

tree.feedback: Rd1+ checks the king along the d-file. The queen sits behind it on d8.
Ra5+ checks, but Black can capture that rook with Qxa5. Use the d-file instead.

steps.explanation: In this practice line, Black moved the king to e5. The d-file is clear from your rook to Black's queen.

question.prompt: Capture the queen with your rook.
hints: Your rook can travel up the clear d-file.

tree.feedback: Rxd8 wins the exposed queen. The king on e5 cannot recapture the rook.
Re1 moves away from the queen. Capture the queen before Black can save it.

takeaway: Line up a rook, bishop, or queen with two targets. A check can force the king to move, exposing a valuable piece behind it.
